# BLO-36854 — close the 128–256 KiB prompt-delivery dead band

[BLO-36854](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-36854) ·
`src/server/job-manifest.ts`, `src/server/job-manifest.test.ts`

Lowered `LARGE_PROMPT_THRESHOLD_BYTES` from 256 KiB to 120 KiB.

The constant was sized against the ~1 MiB PodSpec limit — its own comment said
so — but the binding ceiling is the kernel's. `PROMPT_CONTENT` is a single
`NAME=value` string passed to the init container's `execve`, which Linux caps at
`MAX_ARG_STRLEN` = 32 pages = 131072 B **per string**, independently of the much
larger total arg+env budget. Prompts between that and 256 KiB therefore took the
env-var path straight into an `E2BIG` rejection.

The failure was maximally unhelpful: the pod died in the `write-prompt` init
container before any model turn, so the run could not report its own breakage,
and it mislabelled as `k8s_pod_schedule_failed`
([BLO-33503](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-33503)) — sending
triage at the cluster. Three routines went fully dark this way.

The Secret-volume path is unchanged and already handled everything above the
threshold; this only moves the boundary below what the kernel accepts.

Measured: a 131072 B prompt becomes a 131087 B env string once `PROMPT_CONTENT=`
is prepended, so the band opens just *under* 128 KiB. The remaining gap to
120 KiB is deliberate slack, not wrapper overhead — the prefix is 15 B.

Supersedes the per-field description cap first attempted for this issue
(`40a935374`, reverted in `12b4fdbe5`). That bounded only one of the five
sections joined into the prompt at `job-manifest.ts`, and so failed open on
exactly the case it was written for.
